method.summary: Each O*NET task gets an AI risk and a robotics risk from task-level research data. Tasks are linked to skills through O*NET Detailed Work Activities -> Generalized Work Activities and O*NET's official skills-to-work-activities linkage. A skill's risk in an occupation is the time-share x link-relevance weighted mean of its linked tasks' risks.
method.task_ai_risk: Anthropic Economic Index task penetration (exact task text match) blended 0.75 / 0.25 with the Eloundou et al. GPT-4 task label (beta: E1=1, E2=0.5, E0=0). If a task has no Eloundou label the 0.25 uses the occupation prior (Eloundou occupation dv_beta, else Felten AIOE percentile, else AI composite). Tasks without Anthropic penetration use the Eloundou task label, else the prior.
method.task_robotics_risk: Anthropic "What work can robots do?" tier / 3 (E0=0, E1=0.33, E2=0.67, E3=1; non-physical rated tasks 0), raised to the tier of any cited robot system tagged to that task_id. Tasks not in the Anthropic robot file: 0.5 x (O*NET degree of automation - 1) / 4.
method.task_to_skill_link: relevance(task, skill) = share of the task's DWA links whose GWA is linked to the skill in O*NET 31 essential_skills_to_work_activities / transferable_skills_to_work_activities. Weight = task time_share (Anthropic) x relevance.
method.skill_risk: weighted mean of linked task ai / robotics risk; combined = 1 - (1 - ai)(1 - robotics). If no task of the occupation links to the skill, the occupation's time-weighted task average is used (basis "occupation_average", confidence low).
method.confidence: high: >= 3 linked tasks and >= 70% of tasks with Anthropic task penetration; medium: >= 1 linked task; low: occupation average.
method.bands: safe: combined < 0.3; at_risk: combined >= 0.5; moderate otherwise. safe_skills / at_risk_skills list only skills with importance >= 2.5; the two lists are disjoint and contain skills only (never abilities or knowledge).
method.exposure_vs_task_share_cards: The pathway exposure (skill_risk_summary.occupation_combined, breakdown.target_combined_exposure) is the time-weighted average combined task risk: each task scores 0..1 for AI and robotics and is weighted by its time share. The task-share cards count tasks instead: exposure.ai.task_share.share = share of tasks with any Anthropic usage; exposure.robotics.exposed_task_share = share of tasks rated E1-E3. A job can have a high AI task share (many tasks touched) but lower combined risk (low penetration or little time on them), and vice versa. Each pathway carries task_shares.target / task_shares.current so both measures can be shown side by side.
method.occupation_combined: time-weighted mean of task combined risk (derived.skill_risk_summary.occupation_combined). This is the exposure figure used by the pathway search.
method.pathways: Every occupation is a candidate (O*NET related gets a x1.1 bonus only). safe_overlap = importance x distinctiveness weighted share of the target's required skills (importance >= 2.5, at least the top 6) covered by the user's skills: credit 1 for safe, 0.5 for moderate, 0 for at_risk, times level match (1 at level >= target - 0.5, falling to 0 over 1.5 more points). score = safe_overlap x exposure_factor (1 - target combined exposure) x growth_factor (1 + min(growth%, 20)/40) x gap_factor (1 - 0.5 x min(1, mean level shortfall / 2)) x job_zone_factor x similarity_factor (0.5 + 0.5 x skill-profile cosine) x fit_factor (0.5 + 0.5 x mean of RIASEC-interest and specific-interest-area cosines) x pay_factor (clamp(1 + 0.4 x ln(target/current BLS median wage), 0.5, 1.08); 1 with pay_missing when a wage is missing) x hub_factor (max(0.5, 1 / (1 + 0.4 x ln(1 + appearances / 20))) ^ (1 - 0.5 x skill-profile similarity), so a popular target is damped hard for unrelated sources and barely for closely related ones; O*NET related targets are exempt (hub_factor 1) because the related list is independent evidence the move is real; appearances = sources with the target in their pre-damping top 30) x related_bonus. Eligible only if: target exposure <= source - 0.1 and <= 0.85 x source; BLS 2025-35 growth >= 0; safe_overlap >= 0.3; job zone within +2/-1; skill-profile similarity >= 0.35; interest fit >= 0.1 (when both jobs have interest data); not an ", All Other" code. Slots are filled highest score first across all occupations and no target is kept for more than 10% of occupations. Top 10 kept.
method.tiered_fallback: Every occupation gets at least 3 future_proof_pathways. Tier 1 (tier_label "Strict match") = the rules above. If fewer than 3 tier-1 pathways exist, the list is filled (never replaced) in order: tier 2 "Relaxed thresholds" = same scoring and safe-skill crediting, but exposure drop >= 0.03 and <= 95% of the source, safe_overlap >= 0.15, similarity >= 0.20, no interest-fit cut, target must have a BLS median wage; tier 3 "Broader move (retraining likely)" = any job with strictly lower combined exposure, non-negative BLS growth and a BLS median wage, job zone +2/-2, gating kept (and in tiers 2-3 a job zone 5 or doctoral health target needs a source that is itself job zone 5 or doctoral health), overlap credits every skill at level (breakdown.skill_fit, needs_retraining: true); only for sources at or below 6% exposure that still lack 3 is a target under 10% exposure allowed (similarly low, not necessarily lower, and the reason says so). Tier 3 similarity floor: min(0.10, the source own 90th-percentile similarity to all occupations). MD/DO, DDS/DMD, DC, OD, DPM and DVM practitioner targets (licensed_doctor) are only reachable from the same group, in every tier and in reskilling. Fallback items keep hub damping but not the 10% hard cap, are sorted by tier then score, and every reason starts with "Tier 2" / "Tier 3".
method.gating: Targets in O*NET job zone 5, and licensed doctoral health roles (SOC 29-1xxx whose BLS typical education is a doctoral or professional degree), are only eligible when the source is job zone >= 4 AND in a related family: the same SOC major group, or, for health targets, a health (29) or science (19) source. Applies to future_proof and reskilling pathways.
method.reskilling_pathways: Only for occupations with fewer than 3 future_proof_pathways. Same eligibility, factors, hub damping and cap, but skill_fit credits every skill the user has at level (any risk band), needs skill_fit >= 0.4, and allows at most 4 new skills (target skills with a level gap >= 1). Each item has needs_retraining: true and new_skills[]; never mixed into future_proof_pathways. Top 5.

pathways.distinctiveness: weight = importance x (0.5 + min(2, max(0, importance - mean importance of that skill across all occupations)) / 2)
